sermon.title: The Epistles to the Churches Encouraged Morality
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer surveys the epistles’ call to morality: Romans on creation and same-sex sin, baptism killing the old nature, love fulfilling the law; Corinthian church discipline; Galatians’ true gospel versus moral compromise; Ephesians/Colossians on fathers; and 1 Timothy on the law for the lawless including kidnappers.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Sensitive: Romans 1 same-sex, church discipline for sexual immorality, same-sex marriage as another gospel, murder/insanity defense critique, slavery/kidnapping distinction. Kept as spoken.

chunks.section_question: What gospel does Galatians defend against moral compromise?
chunks.short_answer: Galatians 1:4,8: Jesus delivers from this present evil age; if we or an angel preach another gospel, accursed. Saying same-sex marriage and sin are okay, or excusing murderers as insane without justice, is another gospel. Galatians 5 fruit: love, joy, peace, self-control—against such there is no law.

chunks.section_question: Who is the law made for according to 1 Timothy 1:9?

faqs.question: Do the just live by faith in morals?
faqs.answer: He says they are moral people; live by faith means faith in morals and in the Just One, Jesus.

faqs.question: Is “deserving of death” in Romans 1 physical execution of gossips?
faqs.answer: He asks what death—pointing to eternal death for those practices, not killing backbiters.

faqs.question: Is eating pork a moral issue like sexual sin?
faqs.answer: He says don’t-eat-pork was a shadow law; pork doesn’t affect your spirit the way morals do—morals are the high priority.

faqs.question: Should you mark people who cause divisions contrary to doctrine?
faqs.answer: Romans 16:17: mark those who cause divisions and offenses contrary to the doctrine you learned.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Now I urge you, brethren, note those who cause divisions and offenses, contrary to the doctrine which you learned, and avoid them.

faqs.question: Should believers keep company with sexually immoral so-called brothers?
faqs.answer: 1 Corinthians 5:11—don’t even keep company with them.

scriptures.text_nkjv: But now I have written to you not to keep company with anyone named a brother, who is sexually immoral, or covetous, or an idolater, or a reviler, or a drunkard, or an extortioner—not even to eat with such a person.

faqs.question: How are people judged—by faith label or behavior?
faqs.answer: According to what he has done—his behavior and lifestyle—not according to one’s faith slogan or denomination.

faqs.question: What is the terror of the Lord for?
faqs.answer: A healthy fear to behave so as to avoid eternal damnation in the lake of fire.

faqs.question: What if an angel preaches another gospel?

scriptures.text_nkjv: But even if we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel to you than what we have preached to you, let him be accursed.

faqs.question: Must fathers avoid provoking children?
faqs.answer: Ephesians 6:4 and Colossians 3:21: do not provoke children to anger lest they become discouraged.

faqs.question: Are kidnappers under the law’s condemnation?
faqs.answer: 1 Timothy lists menstealers/kidnappers among those the law is made for; forcing someone is not the same as limited debt service.
